metrics.label: slit center: variance improvement vs best single, equal queries

physical.scope: Selected successes, not a global speedup. Equal queries are not equal time. Both flight lengths lie in [0.12, 3.2], selecting a bounded subset of two-scatter paths. This standalone research harness is not integrated into the production renderer; it excludes all other scattering orders, specular interfaces and camera aperture.
ledger: Emission and first-scatter polar coordinates are sampled with normalized, declared PDFs. All roots are reconstructed and checked against the same finite distance domain. The plane partner retains positive sampling mass rather than switching charts after seeing a bad sample.

Clear and slit ray estimates are checked against an independent physical reference. The hardest difficult reference has roughly 42% relative standard error and a roughly 35% refinement change, so that comparison remains unresolved. Confidence intervals are empirical finite-replicate summaries.

The new beauty and reference pairs use a genuine 640 × 440 camera grid. Atlas films use 1,280 queries/pixel and the independent reference uses 1,024 samples/pixel. The raw arrays, complete scene settings and seeds are retained in a separate hero-film record. No high-resolution image is produced by enlarging a smaller one.

The five original chart comparisons stay at 320 × 220 and 320 queries/pixel, displayed compactly and labeled as such. Their original reference uses 1,024 samples/pixel. Those files and the historical ray benchmarks are unchanged; the 1.72× ray statistic is not a measurement of the new hero images.

All physical films share the same exposure. The beauty view applies bilateral log-radiance filtering and bloom after estimation. This biased display treatment has no spatial upsampling in the new hero, and no display-filtered pixels enter the numerical results.

shadow.title: Shadow Atlas
shadow.kind: Recorded conditional visibility field · false-color display

views.label: Exact openings
views.caption: Actual ray-tested sheet visibility, projected with a fixed color transfer and display glow. Broad openings give nearby primitive coordinates a coherent answer.
views.title: A memory for the openings

views.label: Cached prediction
views.caption: A frozen 384 × 256 cache predicts the same field. In this favorable configuration, measured cache-only integral bias is +0.010%; the cache still changes the target.
views.title: Cached prediction

views.label: Exact correction
views.caption: Prediction plus an occasional signed exact residual. Corrections are retained before display mapping; negative samples are not discarded from the estimator.
views.title: Exact correction

views.label: Fine-slat failure
views.caption: A coarse cache misses fine slats: cache-only integral bias +23.3%. Finding many cheap answers is not useful if they describe the wrong shadow.
views.title: Fine-slat failure

views.label: Fine-slat truth
views.caption: The actual fine-slat visibility field. Compare its narrow openings with the coarse cached prediction.
views.title: Fine-slat truth

views.label: Moved-screen failure
views.caption: The blocker moved, but the old atlas did not. Its silhouette mismatch is 64.4%; this is a deliberate stale-cache failure, not automatic invalidation.
views.title: Moved-screen failure

views.label: Moved-screen truth
views.caption: Exact visibility after the move. Rebuilding fixes the prediction but has a real cost, recorded separately.
views.title: Moved-screen truth

views.label: Signed residual
views.caption: Positive and negative visibility residuals show where the old cache adds light or removes it incorrectly.
views.title: Signed residual

metrics.label: exact queries including cache build / evaluation samples
broad openings: time × variance vs exact (lower is better)
stale cache: same metric becomes worse

shadow.scope: One conditional sheet-to-endpoint visibility leg, not full heterogeneous transport. Timings are CPU/NumPy measurements in this reuse regime, including a cold build; they are not a production-renderer acceleration claim.
ledger: The exact field uses ray intersections against opaque boxes. A fixed atlas stores their visibility in primitive coordinates. The estimator is prediction + Bernoulli(ε)/ε × (exact − prediction), with ε = 0.12.

The cache is frozen during evaluation. Signed corrections are retained in sums; only the finished display is tone-mapped. Fine and stale predictors increase residual variance, even though they use fewer exact queries.

Images sum the actual near and far sheet intersections. Color, rim emphasis and bloom are display choices. The statistics and image quadrature serve different roles; the visible sheet is not a physical volume beauty render.
